A1.justification: Both complete 26-page PDFs describe the same work, Golden Noise for Diffusion Models: A Learning Framework. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support comparison of the main text, Appendices A–F, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original NPNet benchmark evaluations, ablations, generalization tests, and efficiency measurements in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains the original NPNet experiments and their numerical and qualitative outcomes in Section 4 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–3 retain the same noise-pair collection, filtering, singular-value and residual prediction components, training objective, and inference procedure. The appendix proof corrections do not alter the specified method.

E1.justification: Both use Pick-a-Pic, DrawBench, HPD v2, and GenEval. The ImageNet fish-class FID evaluation and ControlNet examples with pose, edge, and depth conditions are also retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Standard, Inversion, and Repaint retain their respective roles in Tables 2–3; DPO and AYS combinations remain in Table 5; and the InitNO comparison remains in Appendix Table 7.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A.4 retain the same training and evaluation sample counts, prompt subsets, metrics, model configurations, guidance scales, sampling steps, epochs, and batch sizes. No experimental protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The architecture and data-selection ablations, hyperparameter and training-size analyses, sampler and seed-range tests, efficiency analyses, and ControlNet case studies are unchanged, including their appendix evidence.

E5.justification: The random-seed descriptions in Section 4 and Appendix D.4/Table 16 are unchanged. Neither repeated-run information nor uncertainty-reporting practices are revised.

E6.justification: All reported numerical scores, plotted results, and qualitative examples are retained. For example, Appendix Table 13 reports the same SDXL GenEval HPSv2 scores in both versions: 24.04 for Standard and 28.41 for NPNet.

T1.justification: Appendix E changes four right-hand-side occurrences of x′_T to x_T across Equations (12)–(14). This corrects the source/target-noise inconsistency in the derivation and aligns its conclusion with Equation (10); the theorem statement, assumptions, and remaining reasoning are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning noise prompt learning, NPD/NPNet, image quality, efficiency, and generalization across diffusion models.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the experimental results and the proposed semantic-injection mechanism are unchanged. Appendix F retains the same limitations concerning data quality, selection bias, rudimentary architecture, and incomplete principled understanding.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit project GitHub link beneath the author information. Implementation settings, pseudocode, example inference code, and the promised dataset release remain unchanged. The PDFs establish the new access pointer but do not establish repository contents or release completeness.

R1.justification: The references and research positioning in the introduction and Appendices B–C are unchanged, including the comparisons with prior noise-optimization approaches and the claimed novelty of formulating noise prompting as a learning problem.

P1.justification: The front matter gains a GitHub line and an updated arXiv version/date stamp. Narrative wording, terminology, section organization, and appendix structure otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added repository line shifts Figure 1 and its caption downward and causes limited abstract/introduction reflow across pages 1–3. Figures and tables retain their content, structure, labels, and captions.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects the source-noise term in Appendix E’s derivation and adds a project repository pointer, improving mathematical consistency and implementation-resource discoverability. These are limited, concrete benefits; the method, empirical evidence, core claims, and stated limitations remain unchanged.
